---
title: "Command line"
---

Installing EvoDAG puts four commands on your `PATH`:

| Command | Purpose |
|:-----------------|:---------------------------------------------------------|
| `EvoDAG-params` | search the parameter space at random and store what it found |
| `EvoDAG-train` | train a model (or an ensemble) and store it in a file |
| `EvoDAG-predict` | load a model and predict a data set |
| `EvoDAG-utils` | inspect models and parameter files, and combine models |

All four accept `-h` / `--help`, `--version` (prints `EvoDAG` and the version), and `--verbose LEVEL`, which sets the level of the `EvoDAG` logger from the standard `logging` module as an integer (10 shows debug messages, 20 informational ones). `-u` / `--cpu-cores` is the number of processes to use.

## A short session

Take a comma separated file `train.csv` without a header, one example per row, the class in the last column, and a file `test.csv` with the same columns except the class.

```bash
# train an ensemble of 30 models with the default parameters
EvoDAG-train -C -n 30 -u 4 -m model.evodag train.csv

# predict the test set, one class per line
EvoDAG-predict -m model.evodag -o predictions.txt test.csv
```

To let EvoDAG look for good parameters first, run the search and give its output to `EvoDAG-train`:

```bash
EvoDAG-params -C -r 734 -u 4 -P params.json train.csv
EvoDAG-train -P params.json -n 30 -u 4 -m model.evodag train.csv
```

## Data formats

### CSV

A CSV file has one example per line and the values separated by commas, with no header line. Blank lines are skipped, and a file whose name ends in `.gz` is read compressed.

* **Training files** (`EvoDAG-params`, `EvoDAG-train`): the *last* column is the target, either a class or, for regression, a real number. A value in a feature column that is not a number is replaced by an integer that identifies that text; the correspondence is stored with the model, so that the same text maps to the same number when predicting.
* **Class labels** that are numbers are used as such. Labels that are text are replaced by integers while training and mapped back to your text by `EvoDAG-predict`. When the labels are numbers the predictions are printed as numbers, for example `1.0`.
* **Files to predict**, and the test set of `EvoDAG-train`: only features, with no target column. The number of columns must not be smaller than the number used for training.
* **Several targets**: with `--output-dim k` the last `k` columns are `k` real targets (see `--output-dim` below).

### JSON

With `-j` / `--json` the file has one JSON object per line. There are two layouts.

The first one gives each feature as a key that is the position of the feature written as a string; features that are missing count as zero, which makes it a convenient way to write sparse data. The target is under the key `klass`. The number of features is the number of keys (minus one for `klass`) unless the object has a key `num_terms`:

```json
{"0": 1.5, "3": 0.25, "klass": "spam", "num_terms": 4}
```

The second layout gives all the features in a list under the key `vec`:

```json
{"vec": [1.5, 0.0, 0.0, 0.25], "klass": "spam"}
```

If an object has both `vec` and `vecsize`, `vec` is read as a list of `[position, value]` pairs of a vector with `vecsize` positions, again sparse. The environment variables `KLASS` and `VEC` change the names `klass` and `vec`.

## `EvoDAG-params`

Samples points from the space of parameters, trains EvoDAG with each one on the training set (three runs with different seeds) and writes the configurations sorted by the median fitness on the validation part, best first. The output is a JSON list; each element is a full set of parameters plus its `fitness` (the three values obtained) and the time that it took. The space that is sampled is `parameter_values.json`, described in [Parameters](parameters.qmd). For classification every configuration has the agreement selection and the random choice of the individual that leaves; with `-R` those two keys are left out.

```bash
EvoDAG-params [-C | -R] [-r N] [-P FILE] [options] training_set
```

| Option | Meaning |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| `training_set` | the training file (positional) |
| `-C`, `--classifier` | the task is classification (one of `-C` or `-R` is required) |
| `-R`, `--regressor` | the task is regression |
| `-r N`, `--optimize-parameters N` | number of points to sample; 734 by default |
| `-P FILE`, `--parameters FILE` | where to write the result; `training_set.EvoDAGparams` if omitted (a name ending in `.gz` is compressed) |
| `--parameters-values FILE` | a JSON file with the values to sample, instead of `parameter_values.json` |
| `--output-dim K` | number of targets at the end of each row; 1 by default |
| `--only-paramsfiles` | do not train anything: write each sampled configuration as `N_params.json` inside a new directory named by `-P` |
| `-e N`, `--early_stopping_rounds N` | fix this parameter to `N` during the search |
| `-p N`, `--popsize N` | fix the population size to `N` during the search |
| `-s N`, `--seed N` | seed of the sampling; 0 by default |
| `--time-limit SECONDS` | fix the time limit |
| `-j`, `--json` | the training file is JSON |
| `-u N`, `--cpu-cores N` | processes to use; 1 by default |
| `--version`, `--verbose LEVEL`, `-h`, `--help` | as for every command |

## `EvoDAG-train`

Trains the model and stores it. Models are stored with `pickle` in a gzip file, together with the correspondence of text values to numbers.

```bash
EvoDAG-train (-C | -R | -P FILE) [-n N] [-m FILE] [options] training_set
```

| Option | Meaning |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| `training_set` | the training file (positional) |
| `-C`, `--classifier` | classification with the default parameters (`default_parameters.json`, described in [Parameters](parameters.qmd): they include the agreement selection and the random choice of the individual that leaves) |
| `-R`, `--regressor` | regression with the default parameters (`default_parameters_r.json`, the ordinary selections) |
| `-P FILE`, `--parameters FILE` | use the parameters of a file written by `EvoDAG-params`; the first configuration (the best) is used. The task is read from the file; `-C`, `-R` and `-P` are mutually exclusive, and one of them is required |
| `--kw JSON` | a JSON object with parameters that override the defaults, for instance `--kw '{"popsize": 500}'` |
| `-n N`, `--ensemble-size N` | number of models in the ensemble; 30 by default. With `-n 1` a single model is trained |
| `-m FILE`, `--model FILE` | where to store the model; the training file name up to its first dot followed by `.evodag.gz` if omitted |
| `-t FILE`, `--test_set FILE` | a test set, in the format of the files to predict, evaluated while the models are trained |
| `-s N`, `--seed N` | seed of the first model (the next ones use the following integers); when omitted, the seed in the parameters is used (0 by default) |
| `--output-dim K` | number of targets at the end of each row; 1 by default. For several real targets use it with `-R` and `--kw '{"multiple_outputs": true}'` |
| `-j`, `--json` | the training file is JSON |
| `-u N`, `--cpu-cores N` | processes used to train the ensemble; 1 by default |
| `--version`, `--verbose LEVEL`, `-h`, `--help` | as for every command |

While an ensemble is trained, the models that are done are written to a directory named after the model file with `_dir` appended, which is removed when the training ends. Because of that, a training that was interrupted can be started again with the same command and goes on from the models that were finished.

## `EvoDAG-predict`

Loads a model written by `EvoDAG-train` and predicts a file.

```bash
EvoDAG-predict -m FILE [-o FILE] [options] test_set
```

| Option | Meaning |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| `test_set` | the file to predict (positional), features only |
| `-m FILE`, `--model FILE` | the model |
| `-o FILE`, `--output-file FILE` | where to write the predictions; `test_set.evodag.csv` if omitted |
| `--predict-proba` | write, for each example, the probability of each class (the fraction of the models that vote for it) |
| `--decision-function` | write the decision function (the median of the models' outputs) instead of the class |
| `--raw-outputs` | write the outputs of every model, side by side |
| `-j`, `--json` | the file to predict is JSON |
| `-u N`, `--cpu-cores N` | processes used to evaluate the models; 1 by default |
| `--version`, `--verbose LEVEL`, `-h`, `--help` | as for every command |

By default the output has one line per example with the class (or, for regression, the predicted value). The other three options write the values of each example in one line, separated by commas. `--predict-proba` and `--raw-outputs` need an ensemble, that is a model trained with `-n` greater than 1.

## `EvoDAG-utils`

A collection of small tools. Which one runs depends on the flag; only the first of these flags found is used, in the order of the table.

```bash
EvoDAG-utils [flag] [-o FILE] model_file
```

| Option | Meaning |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| `model_file` | the model or the parameters file (positional) |
| `-G`, `--graphviz` | write the model in the dot language to the file given with `-o` (for an ensemble `-o` is a directory with one file per model) |
| `--remove-terminals` | with `-G`, leave the input variables out of the graph |
| `-P`, `--params-stats` | `model_file` is a parameters file from `EvoDAG-params`; write to `-o`, as JSON, the most common value of each parameter |
| `--fitness` | print the median error of the models on their validation part |
| `--size` | print the median number of nodes of the models |
| `--height` | print the median height of the models |
| `--used-inputs-number` | print how many different inputs the model uses |
| `--create-ensemble` | `model_file` is a list of model files, separated by spaces, that may contain wildcards; combine them into one ensemble written to `-o` |
| `-n N`, `--ensemble-size N` | with `--create-ensemble`, keep only the `N` models with the best validation fitness; all by default |
| `--best-params-file` | `model_file` is a directory of model files named `K_<anything>.model`, where `K` is the number of a configuration written by `EvoDAG-params --only-paramsfiles` (for instance one model per seed); it prints the name `K_params.json` of the configuration whose models have the best median validation fitness |
| `-o FILE`, `--output-file FILE` | the output file or directory |
| `-u N`, `--cpu-cores N` | processes to use; 1 by default |
| `--version`, `--verbose LEVEL`, `-h`, `--help` | as for every command |
